dataset_family: Beijing Aging Brain Rejuvenation Initiative (BABRI) cohort, Beijing Normal University, Beijing, China
method_family: Atlas-based DTI (FA/MD in 20 JHU white-matter tracts) against whole-brain voxelwise VBM grey-matter volume, in florbetapir-PET-stratified MCI (white-matter diffusion microstructure)
what_it_shows: Dai et al. (2026), Front Neurol 16:1658712. 32 NC, 19 amyloid-negative MCI and 18 amyloid-positive MCI, cross-sectional. Both MCI subgroups had lower FA and higher MD than NC across many tracts (group effects in 14/20 tracts for FA and 16/20 for MD). Voxelwise VBM (p < 0.001 uncorrected, FWE p < 0.05) found significant GM atrophy only in amyloid-positive MCI (bilateral hippocampus, left parahippocampus). Amyloid-negative MCI showed only non-significant atrophy trends, all outside the hippocampus. Amyloid-positive MCI had more left hippocampal atrophy and greater left CH/FMAJ MD than amyloid-negative MCI.
why: Identity: the PDF's title, authors (Dai, Zhang J ... Zhang Z) and DOI 10.3389/fneur.2025.1658712 match the block and the map. I read the whole extract through the limitations and the back matter. STATED = partly. Part shown: in amyloid-negative MCI (n=19), a microstructural measure (WM DTI) separated MCI from NC while GM volume did not reach significance. Not shown: (1) In amyloid-positive MCI, the AD-spectrum group, hippocampal volume WAS significantly reduced and was the main difference between the subgroups, which contradicts 'especially hippocampal' for that group. (2) 'Late' is the authors' literature-based interpretation and is not tested; the design is cross-sectional. (3) No conversion data. NARROWED = partly. The amyloid-negative pattern matches the form ('a non-volumetric measure carried information that volume did not'), but the study's two tests are not like-for-like. DTI was tested in 20 atlas WM ROIs by ANCOVA with FDR (the Figure 2 caption says Bonferroni). GM volume was tested voxelwise over the whole brain with FWE correction, and no hippocampal or other ROI volume test for amyloid-negative MCI vs NC is reported. The tissues also differ (white-matter tracts vs grey matter). So the study does not show, at comparable sensitivity, that volume failed where diffusion succeeded. The same VBM did detect hippocampal atrophy in the similarly sized amyloid-positive group, which gives the null some weight. Further caveats: n=19; the authors call the amyloid-negative WM alterations 'mild'; not all NCs had PET. Independence: BABRI is not the dataset of any current supporter, and no authors are shared with supporters or other candidates. The method family is diffusion MRI (tract DTI), the same broad family as P-581 and candidate P-651. Not a preprint. In the quotes, typographic spaces and dashes are normalised to ASCII.

quotes.quote: Both MCI subgroups exhibited extensive disruptions of WM integrity.

The threshold for the resulting statistical parametric maps was established at p < 0.001 (uncorrected) and then family-wise error (FWE) corrected for multiple comparisons at p < 0.05. Then, the DTI metrics of the atlas-based tract ROIs were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) in which the age, sex, and years of education were treated as covariates.

Overall, a graded pattern of WM disruption was observed, with the Aβneg MCI group showing mild alterations, and the Aβpos MCI displaying more pronounced abnormalities. Figure 2A presents the comparison of FA among three groups, where 14 of the 20 atlas-based WM tract ROIs exhibit significant intergroup differences. Specifically, post-hoc analyses found that both Aβneg MCI and Aβpos MCI patients showed decreased FA in the bilateral cingulum cingulate gyrus part (CCG), cingulum hippocampus part (CH), inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF), right anterior thalamic radiation (ATR), inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF), left uncinate fasciculus (UF), and forceps minor (FMIN).
Similarly, the two MCI subgroups showed extensive increased MD in 16 of the 20 WM tract ROIs.
Relative to NC, Aβpos MCI showed significant atrophy in the bilateral hippocampus (HIP) and left parahippocampus.

In the Aβneg MCI group, an atrophy trend was observed in the right supramarginal gyrus, inferior temporal gyri, left temporal pole, and fusiform gyrus; however, these changes did not reach statistical significance. Relative to Aβneg MCI, Aβpos MCI exhibited more atrophy in the left HIP.
In summary, both MCI subgroups showed widespread WM tract disruptions, whereas significant GM atrophy was observed only in the Aβpos MCI group.
Second, this study adopted a cross-sectional design, which limited the examination of how Aβneg MCI progress over time.
